issues.failure_explanation: Because E_J contains the first J eigenfunctions and λ_J is of order J^{2/d}, the standard tail rate is J^{-γ/d}, not J^{-γ}; the sharp RKHS projection growth is J^{(γ-r)/d}, not J^{γ-r}. Later exponent calculations, including the asserted limit in (quadbd), behave as though these missing factors 1/d were present. With the printed powers, that limit need not hold for the allowed d, γ, and κ, so the posterior perturbation argument is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: \|P_{E_J}\phi - \phi\|_{L^2} \le c \|\phi\|_{\mathcal H} J^{-\gamma},~~\|P_{E_J}\phi\|_{\mathcal H} \le c \max(1,J^{\gamma - r}) \|\phi\|_{H^r}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the projection powers systematically by the rates dictated by λ_J≈J^{2/d}, and recheck every ensuing choice of J_N and exponent limit, in particular the approximation and Cameron–Martin terms in the proof of laplaceapp.
issues.overall_effect: The localization and Cameron–Martin perturbation estimates underlying the functional Bernstein–von Mises theorem are not justified with the stated projection bounds, and consequently the main abstract and reaction-diffusion conclusions are unreliable.
issues.title: Projection rates are inconsistent with the eigenvalue enumeration

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed tail integral corresponds to the event ||θ−θ0||_{H^{-k-2}}>N^{-1/2}, not to the smaller event ||θ−θ0||_{H^{-k-2}}>1 used in the purported upper bound. Replacing the true event by a smaller one cannot upper-bound the integral, so the claimed exponentially small Wasserstein distance does not follow from the calculation.

issues.failure_explanation: Pointwise Taylor expansion gives |m|≤C|u_{θ0+h}−u_{θ0}|^2, hence ||m||_2≤C||u_{θ0+h}−u_{θ0}||_4^2, not C||u_{θ0+h}−u_{θ0}||_2^2. The latter inequality is false for concentrated functions. Thus (inhom) and the L2 Lipschitz estimate (tbdu) do not prove the asserted quadratic remainder in (quadap).

issues.failure_explanation: The concluding argument controls only the conditional Wasserstein distance for Y_N=√N(u_θ−u_{tilde θ_N}). It does not apply the mean limit from mainbvm, the continuous mapping theorem for Du_{θ0}, and a separate nonlinear remainder bound to √N(u_{tilde θ_N}−u_{θ0}). Thus the second asserted convergence is not proved.
